headline: US Dollar Reaches 19-Month High as Australian Dollar Weakens on Jobs Data
summary: The US dollar index held near a 19-month high following hawkish Federal Reserve meeting minutes. The Australian dollar fell to a 10-month low of $0.6692 after Australian employment declined for a second straight month.
why: The US dollar serves as the primary currency for international trade and global financial markets.

impacts.name: AUD/USD
impacts.why: Weaker employment data reduced expectations of rate hikes in Australia, pushing the currency to a 10-month low.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Contrasting labor data in Australia and hawkish Fed signals in the US strengthened the dollar against the Aussie dollar.
